digest.definition: A scientific and reflective discipline studying mind, brain, experience, behaviour and socio-cultural context in human and non-human animals, both theoretical and applied, with roots in philosophy, biology and physics
distinctiveFeatures: A scientific and reflective discipline studying mind, brain, experience, behaviour and socio-cultural context in human and non-human animals, both theoretical and applied, with roots in philosophy, biology and physics
Its aim is psychological literacy: using disciplinary knowledge and insight on real problems, ethically and critically
Ethics is at its core, in research, practice and conduct
It is empirical: progressive laboratory and naturalistic work across quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods, culminating in an independent project
It is evolving and interdisciplinary, and critical of its own historical narrowness of populations and voices
Professional routes run beyond the degree, through the BPS and the HCPC

subjectSpecific.text: You will understand the ideas and history that psychology is built on.
You will be able to look at psychological questions from several angles, knowing that psychology uses many methods, theories, kinds of evidence and ways of applying them.
You will be able to combine ideas and findings from different approaches and use what you know about psychology on real problems, ethically, professionally and safely.
You will be able to spot, put in context and assess the many patterns in how people behave, think and experience the world.
You will be able to think critically about complex problems and come up with creative, new solutions.
You will be able to form your own hypotheses and research questions from theory, research and practice, then design studies and gather new data.
You will be able to use many research methods, such as experiments, observation, questionnaires, tests, interviews, focus groups, creative methods or existing datasets.
You will understand why research done with people, not only on them, matters: participatory and action research, and research led by users, communities and peers.
You will be able to analyse, present and assess numerical, qualitative and mixed data, and question what research findings show.
You will be able to handle, combine and weigh up sources that disagree, such as different studies or theories.
You will be able to reason from evidence and think through the practical, theoretical and ethical questions your research methods raise.
You will be able to use, and judge the limits of, the tools of psychology, such as specialist software, lab equipment and psychometric tests.
You will be able to assess psychological theories and research critically and reflectively.
You will understand how theories are built and be able to ask psychological questions that grow out of theory.
You will carry out a substantial research project of your own, showing that you can plan and design it, deal with its ethical questions, analyse the results and share what you found.

transferable.text: You will be able to communicate well, in speech and in other ways.
You will be able to work with others professionally and respond inclusively to people with different needs and expectations.
You will be able to reason with numbers and analyse, present and interpret numerical data.
You will be able to analyse, interpret and present qualitative data, such as interviews or text.
You will be confident with digital tools: online databases, analysis software and digital ways of developing yourself personally and professionally.
You will understand what artificial intelligence does and how it is used in learning, solving problems and at work.
You will understand the ethical, practical and legal rules for collecting, storing, using and sharing information, including digital information.
You will be able to find and organise information from many kinds of sources and notice whose knowledge and evidence gets heard and whose gets left out.
You will be able to work inclusively with others and reflect on why hearing different views helps a group agree on solutions.
You will be able to reflect on and explain your own strengths and what you need to develop, and work out how to do it.
You will take charge of your own learning, career readiness and development, planning your time and managing projects well.

statements.appliesTo: anyone seeking to practise as a psychologist
statements.paraphrase: Practising as a psychologist needs postgraduate study and supervised training beyond the degree; by law anyone using one of the nine protected practitioner titles must be on the HCPC register and have finished an HCPC-approved training course.

forPractitioner.text: An undergraduate or conversion degree does not by itself lead to a protected title: anyone using one of the nine practitioner psychologist titles (Health Professions Order 2001) must be an HCPC registrant who has completed approved training.

forBeneficiary.text: If you want to work as a practitioner psychologist (clinical, forensic, educational and others), you must first complete further postgraduate study and supervised training and register with the professional regulator: the titles are protected by law.

statements.about: equality, diversity and inclusion in personal and professional life
statements.paraphrase: Equality is advanced by learning, teaching and assessment that widen opportunity, remove discrimination and question inaccurate accounts of people; graduates are expected to value equality, diversity and inclusion and carry them into their lives and work.

forPractitioner.text: Learning, teaching and assessment that widen opportunity and challenge biased narratives in the discipline are the means; the expected result is that graduates will value equality, diversity and inclusion and act on them in their personal and professional lives.

forBeneficiary.text: You will come to value equality, diversity and inclusion and build them into how you live and work, helping to make society fairer.

statements.paraphrase: The Equality Act 2010 requires providers to anticipate the accessibility needs of disabled students across teaching, learning, assessment and student life, and accessibility must be considered when courses are designed.

statements.paraphrase: Ethics sits at the core of the discipline and of course design, with activities that apply it to research, practice and daily conduct; students will be able to apply ethics to their own behaviour and judge the ethical conduct of others critically.

forPractitioner.text: Ethics is often at the heart of course design, with activities that bring it into research, practice and daily life; students will be able to act ethically themselves and critically judge the ethics of others.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to apply ethical principles to how you behave in research, in practice and day to day, and to judge critically how ethically others act.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to understand how theory is developed, apply that process, and frame psychological questions driven by theory.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand and use the process of theory development and can frame theory-driven psychological questions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how theories are built and be able to ask psychological questions that grow out of theory.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to complete a substantial independent empirical study that shows, for each student, research skills from design and planning, through ethical questions, to analysis and dissemination.

forPractitioner.text: Each graduate will complete an extensive independent empirical project demonstrating research skills across design, planning, ethics, analysis and dissemination.

forBeneficiary.text: You will carry out a substantial research project of your own, showing that you can plan and design it, deal with its ethical questions, analyse the results and share what you found.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to communicate well by verbal and non-verbal means.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will communicate effectively through a range of verbal and non-verbal means.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate well, in speech and in other ways.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to deal with others professionally and respond inclusively, attentive to the needs and expectations of varied audiences.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will interact professionally and respond inclusively, sensitive to the needs and expectations of diverse audiences.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work with others professionally and respond inclusively to people with different needs and expectations.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show numerical reasoning, including analysing, presenting and interpreting quantitative data.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate numerical reasoning: analysing, presenting and interpreting quantitative data.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reason with numbers and analyse, present and interpret numerical data.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show that one can analyse, interpret and present qualitative data.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate that they can analyse, interpret and present qualitative data.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to analyse, interpret and present qualitative data, such as interviews or text.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to show digital literacy by using online databases, analysis software and digital tools for personal and professional development.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will demonstrate digital literacy: online databases, analysis software and digital tools for their own personal and professional growth.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be confident with digital tools: online databases, analysis software and digital ways of developing yourself personally and professionally.

statements.about: artificial intelligence in learning and work
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to understand what artificial intelligence does and its role in learning, teaching, problem-solving and working practice.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand what artificial intelligence does and where it fits in learning and teaching, problem-solving and working practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand what artificial intelligence does and how it is used in learning, solving problems and at work.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to understand the ethical, practical and legal questions in collecting, managing, storing, processing, sharing and presenting information, digital information included.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will understand the ethical, practical and legal issues across the life of information, from collection to presentation, including in digital formats.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand the ethical, practical and legal rules for collecting, storing, using and sharing information, including digital information.

statements.about: finding information and recognising whose knowledge counts
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to find and organise information from varied sources, academic and non-academic, while recognising the perspectives and influences that raise up or push aside some kinds of knowledge and evidence.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will retrieve and organise information from academic, policy and non-academic sources and recognise the influences that amplify or marginalise particular knowledge and evidence.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to find and organise information from many kinds of sources and notice whose knowledge and evidence gets heard and whose gets left out.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to work inclusively and collaboratively, and reflect on the worth of engaging with differing views when reaching agreed solutions.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will work inclusively and collaboratively and reflect on the value of engaging varied views when reaching consensus on solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work inclusively with others and reflect on why hearing different views helps a group agree on solutions.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to reflect on and explain one's own strengths and areas to develop, and how to address them.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will reflect on and articulate their strengths and development needs and identify how to address them.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reflect on and explain your own strengths and what you need to develop, and work out how to do it.

statements.paraphrase: Will be able to take charge of one's own learning, employability and development, including personal planning and project management.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will take ownership of their learning, employability and development, including personal planning and project management.

forBeneficiary.text: You will take charge of your own learning, career readiness and development, planning your time and managing projects well.

statements.about: conversion course outcomes and framework levels
statements.paraphrase: Assessments matched to learning outcomes let students reach the standard; the base classification corresponds to framework level 6 (FHEQ, outside Scotland) or level 10 (FQHEIS, Scotland); the standards guide conversion courses at FHEQ level 7 or FQHEIS level 11, whose outcomes must ultimately align with the right framework levels.

forPractitioner.text: These standards are a reference point for conversion courses, but a conversion course's outcomes must ultimately align with FHEQ level 7 or FQHEIS level 11.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in setting outcome levels

statements.paraphrase: Will have named the core areas of psychology and the settings where each can be applied.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have named the discipline's core areas and the settings where each applies.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have identified the main areas of psychology and where each can be used.

statements.paraphrase: Will have reviewed and assessed the key psychological literature systematically.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have systematically reviewed and evaluated the key literature.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have worked through and assessed the key research writing in psychology in a systematic way.

statements.paraphrase: Will have understood how the areas of psychology relate and compared the perspectives within it.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have understood how areas of psychology interrelate and compared perspectives within the discipline.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will understand how the areas of psychology connect and be able to compare its different perspectives.

statements.paraphrase: Will have grasped the part evidence plays in reaching conclusions in psychology.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have appreciated the role of evidence in reaching conclusions.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will understand why evidence matters when drawing conclusions in psychology.

statements.paraphrase: Will have understood the principles and protocols of psychological investigation and followed the relevant legal, ethical and professional guidance.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have understood the principles and protocols of psychological investigation and applied legal, ethical and professional guidelines.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will know the rules and procedures for psychological research and have followed the legal, ethical and professional guidance that applies.

statements.paraphrase: Will have formed and tested hypotheses and carried out supervised research on defined questions, alone and in groups.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have constructed and tested hypotheses and undertaken supervised research, individually and in groups.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have built and tested hypotheses and carried out supervised research on set questions, on your own and with others.

statements.about: summarising findings from quantitative and qualitative methods
statements.paraphrase: Will have summarised findings from quantitative and qualitative methods and understood what they add to knowledge.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have summarised quantitative and qualitative findings and understood their contribution to knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have summed up results from numerical and qualitative research and understood what they add to what we know.

statements.about: hardware and software for learning and research
statements.paraphrase: Will have used suitable hardware and software for study and research.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have used suitable equipment and software in their study and research.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have used the right equipment and software for your study and research.

statements.paraphrase: Will have conveyed psychological knowledge and findings in several formats.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will have communicated psychological knowledge and findings in a range of formats.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold standard, you will have shared psychological knowledge and research findings in different formats.

statements.about: breadth of the discipline and its impact
statements.paraphrase: Will have understood how wide psychology is and how it can make a difference to many real problems.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have grasped how broad psychology is and how it can bear on many real-world challenges.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will understand how broad psychology is and how it can help with many real-world problems.

statements.about: in-depth literature review and history of ideas
statements.paraphrase: Will have reviewed the literature in depth, reflected on historical concepts and theories, and traced what they mean for thinking now.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have conducted in-depth literature reviews, reflected on historical concepts and theories, and explored their bearing on current thinking.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have reviewed research in depth, thought about older ideas and theories, and worked out what they mean for today.

statements.paraphrase: Will have taken several perspectives and analysed research paradigms, methods and measures systematically.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have adopted multiple perspectives and systematically analysed paradigms, methods of enquiry and measurement techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have looked at psychology from several viewpoints and analysed its research approaches, methods and measures carefully.

statements.paraphrase: Will have reflected on how evidence supports conclusions and on scientific reasoning in psychology.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have reflected on the role of evidence and on scientific reasoning.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have thought carefully about how evidence supports conclusions and how to reason scientifically in psychology.

statements.about: research questions and competence across methods
statements.paraphrase: Will have set and critiqued research questions in a way that shows competence in many quantitative and qualitative methods.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have posed and critiqued research questions and shown competence across a wide range of quantitative and qualitative methods.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have set and questioned research questions and shown you can use many numerical and qualitative methods well.

statements.paraphrase: Will have started and finished psychological enquiries while recognising their theoretical, practical and methodological limits.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have initiated and completed enquiries, recognising their theoretical, practical and methodological limitations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have started and finished your own research, aware of its theoretical, practical and method limits.

statements.paraphrase: Will have drawn conclusions from findings, judging their psychological importance, allowing for the diversity of individual experience and proposing further research.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have drawn conclusions from findings, weighed their significance with regard to diverse individual experience, and recommended further investigation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have drawn conclusions from your findings, judged how much they matter, taken account of how differently people experience things, and suggested what to study next.

statements.about: consequences of tools and theoretical choices
statements.paraphrase: Will have understood what follows from using different subject hardware and software and from taking different theoretical positions.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have understood the implications of choosing different subject-relevant hardware and software and different theoretical perspectives.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will understand how your choice of equipment, software and theory shapes your work.

statements.paraphrase: Will have shared research findings with peers and supervisors, adapting communication to what each audience needs.

forPractitioner.text: At the typical level, graduates will have disseminated findings to peers and supervisors, tailoring communication to each audience.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the typical standard, you will have shared your research with fellow students and supervisors, adjusting how you communicate to suit each audience.

statements.about: precise technical discussion of the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have shown precise technical discussion of the nature of psychology, picking out possible misreadings.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have discussed the nature of psychology with technical precision and identified likely misinterpretations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently discussed what psychology is with technical precision, pointing out where it is often misunderstood.

statements.about: original reviews and the limits of understanding
statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have produced original theoretical and practical reviews, found where psychological understanding runs out, challenged myths and offered other readings.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have produced original theoretical and practical reviews, identified the limits of current understanding, challenged myths and offered alternative interpretations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently written original reviews of what psychology knows, shown where that knowledge stops, challenged myths and offered other explanations.

statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have interpreted a wide range of evidence within and beyond psychology's sub-specialisms, making significant connections and applying knowledge comprehensively.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have interpreted evidence across sub-specialisms and related disciplines, made significant connections and applied knowledge comprehensively.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently made sense of wide-ranging evidence across areas of psychology and beyond, linking it in significant ways and applying it thoroughly.

statements.about: critical evaluation of evidence for novel conclusions
statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have shown critical thinking and judged the rigour and weight of evidence in reaching new conclusions.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have shown critical thinking and evaluated the rigour and significance of evidence when reaching novel conclusions.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently thought critically, judging how strong and important evidence is when reaching new conclusions of your own.

statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have expressed complex arguments and concepts clearly and even-handedly.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have articulated complex arguments and concepts coherently and in a balanced way.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently explained complex arguments and ideas clearly and fairly.

statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have designed research creatively, relevant to current psychological issues.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have shown creativity in designing research relevant to contemporary issues.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently designed creative research that speaks to current issues in psychology.

statements.about: findings in social, political and ethical debate
statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have reflected on what historical and current findings mean when brought to social, political and ethical debates and policy.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have weighed what past and present findings mean for social, political and ethical debate and policy.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently thought about what past and present findings mean for social, political and ethical debates and policies.

statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have understood the value of personal and professional skills and acquired transferable employability skills, such as command of particular hardware and software and analytical ability.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have shown they value personal and professional skills and have built transferable employability skills, such as command of particular tools and strong analysis.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently shown that you value personal and professional skills and built skills employers want, such as mastery of particular tools and strong analysis.

statements.about: conveying a comprehensive grasp to varied audiences
statements.paraphrase: Will consistently have conveyed to peers, tutors, supervisors and mixed audiences a full grasp of how psychology informs public debate and decisions.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates will consistently have shown peers, staff and wider audiences a full command of how psychology informs public debate and decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the excellent standard, you will have consistently shown fellow students, tutors and wider audiences a thorough grasp of how psychology shapes public debate and decisions.

statements.paraphrase: It matters that postgraduate award titles reflect achievement and the field studied truthfully; the course provider must make sure students know that HCPC-regulated professions have titles protected by law that only registrants may use.

forPractitioner.text: It matters that postgraduate titles reflect the field and level honestly; and the provider must make sure students know that HCPC-regulated psychology professions carry legally protected titles open only to registrants.

summary.text: The benchmark frames progression as building towards threshold-level subject-specific and transferable skills as students move from one level of study to the next (2.7), with increasing independence and responsibility for one's own learning as students advance towards their future professional careers (3.23). Graduates are expected to take ownership of their own learning, employability and development (3.17), and typical/excellent attainment is partly distinguished by depth of engagement in research and independent study (4.6) and by gaining transferable employability skills (4.10).

summary.text: No statement in this benchmark meets QV-TAG-2's test for the referencing pathway. A mechanical scan against the pathway's term list, and a second, independent manual search for referencing/citation/plagiarism/academic-integrity language, both found only false positives (for example 'reference point', 'reflective'). This benchmark makes no explicit statement about students referencing or citing sources, and that absence is itself recorded here rather than left silent.

Course content and design emphasise critical thinking throughout (1.20), including students who think critically about dominant systems of thought (1.21) and critically evaluate the ethical behaviour of others (2.5). Critical appraisal also appears in specific research and disciplinary contexts, such as psychometric tests (3.9) and research design (3.10), and graduates are expected to critically and reflectively evaluate psychological theory and research (3.16). Attainment above threshold level is distinguished partly by systematic analysis of research paradigms (4.9) and demonstrated use of critical-thinking skills to evaluate the rigour of evidence (4.10).
